alex: quick heads-up — I enabled a bigger KV prefill window in staging to try and cut decode tail latency. after ~1h of mixed load we started seeing workspace fragmentation + intermittent OOMs on the 80GB nodes :grimacing:

alex: profiler snapshot (abridged):
```
GPU0 total 80GB, reserved 72GB
active allocations: 1845
largest-free-chunk: 1.2GB
free-fragments: [512MB, 256MB, 128MB, 64MB, 32MB x 8, 16MB x 12]
fragmentation_ratio = 0.37
kv_cache_prefill_peak = 6.3GB/request
streaming_decode_peak = 4.1GB/request
workspace_highwater = 9.6GB (per-worker)
OOM events: 3 in last hour (OOM during prefill + canary decode)
```

alex: notes: when kernel-selector picked the new fused-attn kernel we saw a transient bump in temp workspace usage (about +700MB/request) which pushed fragmentation over the threshold.

maria: do you have the exact config you flipped? was it just prefill size or also kernel-selector flags?

alex: flipped two things: increased kv_prefill_limit_tokens from 1024 -> 4096 and enabled 'fused_attn_v2' in runtime/kernel_preference. also set per-request kv cap disabled (we removed the legacy per-request cap during prior perf pass).

sam: hmm. that explains it — bigger prefill + new kernel = higher transient temps. fragmented allocator + no per-request cap is a perfect storm. suggestion: re-enable a conservative per-request prefill cap (e.g., 3k tokens) while we tune allocator pooling.

nirav: agree. also we should try enabling buffer reuse/pool aggressively rather than growing workspace. allocator knobs I can try in staging: 
```env
RED_ALLOC_POOL_ENABLED=1
RED_ALLOC_MAX_RESIZE_FACTOR=1.25
RED_ALLOC_MIN_REUSE=1
RED_ALLOC_FRAGMENTATION_ALERT=0.3
RED_KV_PER_REQ_CAP_TOKENS=3072
```
these reduce resize churn and encourage reuse of recently freed buffers.

alex: will test those envs. my preliminary run with pool enabled reduced new allocations by ~22% but fragmentation didn't drop much because prefill requests allocate large contiguous chunks which leave small leftover fragments.

maria: can we change prefill strategy to favor decode-time allocation? i.e., allocate smaller prefix + stream remaining tokens (prefill vs decode tradeoff). even a 25% reduction in prefill size might avoid large contiguous allocations.

sam: yes — implement a hybrid: prefill up to X tokens (fast path) and for longer contexts fall back to streaming prefill+decode so we never allocate >Y contiguous for prefill. also add per-request kv quota enforced in the request layer.

alex: here's a possible policy matrix I sketched:
```
if request.kv_tokens <= 1024: do full prefill (fast)
elif request.kv_tokens <= 3072: do partial prefill (1024) + streaming remainder
else: streaming-only prefill + decode (no contiguous allocation > 2GB)
```

nirav: sounds good. also want to surface fragmentation metrics to the console (per-node free-fragment histogram) so SRE can set auto-throttle rules when fragmentation_ratio > 0.35.

infra-bot: deploy queued: feature/kv-prefill-throttle -> staging (canary 10%) :rocket: scheduled in 7m

qa-bot: running targeted stress now with mix=chat(60%)/embed(30%)/batch(10%), will report OOMs and 95p latency after 30m.

maria: quick perf regression check — we need to ensure adding per-request caps doesn't increase 95p decode lat by >5%. check kernel-selector fallback: prefer lower-temp kernels for high-prefill requests.

sam: note — our bucketed allocator currently merges adjacent free blocks lazily; aggressive coalescing might help but costs CPU on the critical path. another option: maintain a separate large-block pool specifically for KV prefill to avoid fragmenting general-purpose workspace.

alex: +1 on large-block pool. that might be the cleanest: prefill requests grab from large-pool (size classes: 2GB, 1GB, 512MB) and we keep those buckets isolated. small allocations still served by default pool.

nirav: action items I have: (1) enable RED_ALLOC_POOL_ENABLED and RED_KV_PER_REQ_CAP_TOKENS=3072 in staging, (2) add large-block pool prototype behind flag, (3) add fragmentation histogram telemetry.

alex: I'll revert the kv_prefill_limit_tokens change in prod configs and gate fused_attn_v2 behind canary until allocator tweaks land.

maria: QA/infra — keep watch for regression on tail latency. if fragmentation_ratio > 0.4 or OOMs > 1/hr, autoscale to extra nodes and rollback prefill knob.

sam: also let's add a lightweight profiler probe that logs 'temp_workspace_peak' per request in dev logs (sample 1/1000) so we can correlate kernels -> temp peaks.

alex: will push that probe. thanks all. short plan: throttle prefill (per-req cap), enable pool, large-block pool prototype, add histograms + probe, iterate on kernel prefs.

maria: :thumbsup: update this thread when you have staging numbers from the qa run.

sam: ping me if you want help wiring the per-request quota into the gateway — I can PR a quick middleware.

alex: will do; posting initial staging results in this thread in ~45m.
